findings.problem: A status note in the hook is written in the present tense about an event nine days after the draft. It will read wrong almost as soon as the page can go live: editing, verification, images and DJ's publish step all come after October 31. The same wording appears in settle signal 2 ("when she hosts _Saturday Night Live_", where the body gives no date at all) and in the settle FAQ ("when she hosts Saturday Night Live on October 31, 2026"). C128's trigger says to change the tense "after 2026-10-31", but the only scheduled reopen is next_review 2027-02-01, so the stale tense would sit in the opening and the FAQ for three months. The hosting gig also does nothing for the personality argument in the hook. It matters only as a settle catalyst.
findings.acceptance_test: The hook either drops the SNL sentence or words it so it is true both before and after the date (e.g. "was booked to host _Saturday Night Live_ on October 31, 2026"). The body's settle signal 2 carries the absolute date in the same tense-neutral form. The settle FAQ is worded the same way. The C128 and C165 passages are updated to match. No sentence in the body or metadata uses a present or future tense for an event dated before the planned publish or review date.

assessment: Five-year test: passes, provided the fixes above are made. With the latest events removed (the SNL booking, the January 21, 2027 nominations date, the box-office figure), the open-case argument still stands: she leads with named fear and pre-set protection, credibility is the motive she states most plainly, and no episode yet separates the two. Even dropping the October 21, 2026 Buchanan interview weakens but does not collapse the Three case. Three still has the Twitch "take me seriously" fear (Variety, July 2026), the "good job" Oscar safety net, Awards Chatter's "show them", and the 2021 "110%" pact. Dates are absolute almost everywhere: the press campaign is dated to May 2026, every childhood telling has its outlet and month, and the 2023 cut is dated. Changing facts (gross, budget, type self-identification, Oscar date, colleague testimony) are tracked with triggers. Under the open-case durability anchor, what the page calls known would stay true if a later run settled on Three. The settle signals are concrete and observable. Gaps: the SNL tense in the hook, settle signal and FAQ; quotes resting only on a day-old, machine-transcribed podcast recorded as stable with no trigger; a next_review that skips the first catalyst; one section opener dated by when evidence arrived; and two undated absence claims. Metadata: the title's "Obsession's Nikki" ties her identity to the breakout. That stays true but may age as later roles land, which is acceptable now. The "Inde Navarrette Kyle Buchanan" keyword chases a passing search, which is harmless. Similarity: the diagnostic tripped only on triad vocabulary ("whose core emotion is fear/shame") and the open-case formula ("held loosely at low confidence"). That is ordinary type vocabulary and standard phrasing, not reused argument, so I raised no finding. The argument itself (the confession and the refusal, the four childhood tellings, playback vs Twitch) is specific to her.
